messages:
jing: Heads-up — I sketched a small proposal for detecting "orphan" spans (spans that never get stitched to a request/billing key) and a low-cost backfill/recovery path. want quick eyes before i file an RFC.

jing: Problem: ~0.3% of traces in prod show spans with no tenant/billing_key attached (edge proxies dropping header, mobile legacy SDK, sampling race). this leaks cost and makes per-tenant billing and SLOs inaccurate.

ben: curious — how do we differentiate true orphan vs intentionally dropped PII spans?

jing: good q. plan is heuristic-first: if span has trace_id + parent chain but missing billing_key and we can find a coincident request log (same trace_id or same trace window) within +-5s linking to a tenant, mark candidate. PII-only spans will often be redacted and won't have matchable metadata.

marta: sketch the detection rule pls (regex/psuedo).

jing: pasted snippet: ```json
{
  "window_ms": 5000,
  "match_keys": ["trace_id","ingress_request_id"],
  "min_confidence": 0.7
}
```

alex: ok. two tradeoffs i see: 1) doing this at ingest-time adds cpu/lookup cost (join w/ request logs) 2) backfilling later means storage + query complexity. which path are you leaning to?

jing: leaning hybrid: detect orphan spans at ingest cheaply (mark with orphan_candidate=true) and asynchronously run a backfill job that performs a best-effort join against request logs and user-activity events. only promote to billing_key when confidence >= threshold.

katie: what's confidence formula? and how do we avoid double-billing during eventual promotion?

jing: confidence is a small scoring function: exact trace_id match = +0.6, timestamp proximity <1s = +0.2, matching client_ip or user_agent heuristics = +0.1. promote only if >=0.8. to avoid double-billing we will: 1) write promotion as idempotent update that sets billing_key only if null, 2) write an audit event to an append-only log for reconciliation.

ben: about that idempotent update — we need a consistency window. if two backfill workers try to promote different tenants for same trace, how do we decide?

jing: we prefer last-writer-wins based on job coordinator monotonic token (job-run-id + score). but add a tie-breaker: prefer the higher score; if equal, prefer the earliest ingested candidate. not perfect but pragmatic.

marta: can we surface these candidates in console as a first-class telemetry item (orphan-rate per service)? would help customers debug SDK issues.

jing: yep — plan to emit a metric orphan_spans.{service}.rate and a sample traces dashboard with examples. also add a sampling flag so we don't retain too many examples.

sre-bot: deploy-check — note: any ingest-time lookup will add ~0.8ms p50 to span path if we hit the index. marking only (no lookup) is fine.

alex: sounds reasonable. only ask is to measure e2e: added ingest latency, backfill CPU cost, and delta in billing accuracy. can we prototype on a small tenant cohort first?

jing: yes — rollout plan in notes: (A) opt-in pilot for 5 internal tenants w/ detailed logs, (B) run backfill offline for 7 days and compare billing deltas, (C) if <0.1% divergence, flip to opt-out.

katie: what about security/compliance — we might be reattaching PII-like metadata. need privacy review before promotion.

jing: agreed. promotion will never copy raw PII fields. we only attach tenant_id / billing_key which is already a mapping produced by our auth service. will file with security for formal OK.

liz: question on observability side: will this change our existing cost attribution tables / schema? or will we just add a billing_key column update?

jing: minimal schema change: billing_key currently nullable on spans. backfill job issues conditional update. we will add an audit table orphan_backfill_jobs with job_id, trace_id, old_billing_key, new_billing_key, score, worker_id (this is append-only).

ben: runtime perf — can we TTL orphan_candidate marks if no backfill match after 30d so we don't bloat indexes?

jing: yes TTL 30d, and sampling retention for example traces 1% after 7d.

marta: 👍 Can you add a short checklist for RFC: metrics to measure, rollout gates, privacy signoff, SRE cost budget?

jing: adding checklist now and will open the RFC by EOD. TL;DR action items: 1) jing: draft RFC + backfill job code sketch 2) alex: perf microbenchmarking for ingest mark vs lookup (due +3d) 3) katie: security review kickoff (due +5d) 4) ben: dataset retention constraints review (due +5d) 5) marta: console mockups for orphan metric (due +7d).

alex: one more: consider an emergency revert flag (feature flag) that prevents promotions if rollouts break billing flows.

jing: will add feature flag and a one-click revert to the ops playbook.

marta: thanks — this actually helps a lot. :+1:

ben: small nit — update the heuristic table to include mobile SDK version mapping (many old SDKs are common culprits).

jing: noted. i'll include SDK fingerprints in the next diff. planning to open thread RFC link once posted.

liz: fyi, i'll sync with billing team tomorrow to make sure promotion semantics are acceptable.

jing: thanks all — will post RFC link here when done. :rocket:
